_comment: P4 module-seam fixture geometry. Every swatch is painted ONLY if a TurboModule returned the expected value, so a module that is absent, unreachable from JS, or returning a default leaves BACKGROUND at that probe. The gate reads these coordinates and the fixture renders from them, so the two cannot drift.

appearance._comment: Painted green only if Appearance.getColorScheme() === the scheme the engine was told to report (--color-scheme dark). A hardcoded 'light' default — which is what you get if the module is missing and RN falls back — paints RED. Asserting the NON-default value is the point: expecting 'light' would pass without the module existing at all.

statusBar._comment: StatusBarManager is getEnforcing'd at import by NativeStatusBarManagerIOS.js. If it is absent the BUNDLE THROWS and nothing renders at all — so this swatch existing is itself the assertion. Painted from the module's own getConstants().HEIGHT (0 on desktop), proving we read the module rather than a literal.

alert._comment: Painted only after Alert.alert()'s callback fires. The engine has no dialog, so it records the alert and invokes the callback with button 0; a module that did nothing would leave the promise pending and this swatch background. Paired with the native-side alerts_shown counter: pixels prove JS got the callback, the counter proves native was actually reached.

linking._comment: canOpenURL('https://example.com') must be TRUE and canOpenURL('file:///etc/passwd') must be FALSE. Both are required to paint: a predicate stuck on true is as broken as one stuck on false, and a one-sided assertion cannot tell them apart.

initialUrl._comment: Linking.getInitialURL() must resolve to the exact string the engine was launched with (--initial-url). A module returning null would be indistinguishable from 'no URL was passed' if the fixture asserted null, so the gate passes a real one.

devSettings._comment: getEnforcing'd like StatusBarManager. Calling a no-op method must not throw; painting proves the call returned.

defaults._comment: The DELEGATION assertion. NativePerformance is vended by RN's own DefaultTurboModules, NOT by our registry — P2 hand-rolled three of those modules by name and was therefore silently missing this one. Painted only if global.performance.now() returns a positive number, i.e. the delegation fallthrough actually works.

platformConstants._comment: Platform.constants must come FROM the PlatformConstants TurboModule, not from a JS literal. The shim returned {} until P4 while the native module answered correctly — Platform.Version read 0 and nothing indicated the two were unconnected. Asserts the RN version the ENGINE reports (its compiled-in pin), which a JS-side fake could not know.

text._comment: The color scheme rendered as TEXT, so the frame is human-readable and a reviewer can see WHICH scheme was reported rather than just that a square is green.
